title: Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd
capsule: The Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd was proclaimed in January 1926 when Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud conquered Mecca and Medina, absorbing the former Hashemite Kingdom of Hejaz into his already-held Sultanate of Nejd and its Dependencies. Ibn Saud had captured Riyadh from the rival Al Rashid clan in 1902 and steadily expanded Wahhabi-aligned Saudi rule across the peninsula, defeating Sharif Husayn's son Ali at Jeddah in December 1925. The unified kingdom was renamed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by royal decree on 23 September 1932, a date still commemorated as Saudi National Day. During its brief existence the kingdom consolidated Wahhabi religious authority over Islam's holiest sites while negotiating diplomatic recognition from Britain and other powers through the Jeddah Treaty of 1927.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The borders of this kingdom were poorly defined and never formally demarcated; frontier zones with Transjordan, Iraq, and Yemen were subjects of ongoing negotiation, making precise territorial mapping an approximation.
